<reason>Both sides built coherent, well-grounded cases, but B controlled the decisive clash. A's best route was turning B's "holder pays the photocopy" into a concession of funded provenance work, and A pressed it hard; however, B parried with a defensible distinction—surrendering stolen records (postage) versus funding research programs, translation, and museum infrastructure (patronage)—and crystallized it memorably as "the line between property and empire." B's strongest unanswered argument was that unconditional, recipient-defined, unaudited funding cannot survive contact with real treasuries: conditions and consultants inevitably return through the finance ministry, making funded restitution trusteeship by another name. A's decommissioning analogy asserted recipient control but never resolved who funds an uncapped program no parliament will write blind. B also supplied a real accountability mechanism for the clean break (retained records are still stolen property, litigable and shameable), which A dismissed rhetorically but did not dismantle. B answered both pressure questions cleanly; A answered both but leaned on assertions. A additionally incurred execution costs: three of five turns (opening, Rebuttal 2, closing) were clipped for exceeding word limits, cutting off the opening's rebuttal of the opposing view and the closing's final weighing. B's speeches were tighter, better adapted round to round, and made the final choice easier to see.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>The provenance-archive exchange: A's pressure question forced B to concede the holder pays to copy the ledgers, and A's closing weaponized it ("you have accepted funded restitution and renamed it"). B's rebuttal and closing drew the surviving line—copying what was stolen is completing the return, while funding scholarship, labs, and capacity is patronage—paired with the finance-ministry argument that money without strings inevitably regrows conditions. B's parry held; A's concession-turn did not fully capture the motion's conservation and capacity components.</best_rebuttal>
